newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela 12-mo inflation to June slows to 43.5pct.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela 12-mo inflation to June slows to 43.5pct.

text.p: Venezuelan inflation in the twelve months to June 1997 fell to 43.5 percent from 108.1 percent over the same period the year before, the Central Bank said.

The bank confirmed June's 1.8 percent inflation rate -- the second lowest in five years -- that Central Bank president Antonio Casas Gonzalez told journalists earlier Tuesday, ahead of the official data release.
June's rate is down from 3.1 in May and 7.1 percent last year, and brings accumulated inflation over the first six months of the year to 14.6 percent versus 62.3 percent last year.
The market had expected around 2.6 percent for June
"The results achieved so far (this year) are consistent with our objectives of bring inflation significantly down in 1997," the Central Bank said.

Casas earlier told journalists June's good result was due to "a more rational fiscal policy, effective Central Bank open market operations and evidently demand that has not re-activated as expected due to the slow-growing economy."
Casas added Venezuela was now on-track to hit its 30 percent year end inflation target. "Anyone who thinks we can't make 30 percent inflation for this year is wrong," Casas said.

According to the Central Bank, which measures the indicator based on a survey of prices among a broad range of goods and services in the capital, the category clothing and shoes registered the highest price rises in June at 2.2 percent.
This was followed by foods, drinks and tobacco at 2.0 percent, various expenditures at 1.8 percent, and household expenditures at 1.6 percent.

Many analysts expect increased government spending, in large part due to a 70 percent public sector wage increase and a recent $8 billion labor reform, to boost 1997 year end inflation to upwards of 40 percent.
